---
title: "Data imputation"
description: "Inspect missing-value patterns and apply an explicit imputation strategy."
---

## Why this is a separate step

Proteomics missingness can arise from abundance limits, identification uncertainty, stochastic sampling, or technical failures. ProtVis therefore keeps missing values as `NA` until the user explicitly chooses an imputation method.

Before imputation, the current module coerces quantitative columns to numeric, converts non-finite values to missing, and handles not-observed sentinels such as `0` and `-8` as `NA`.

## Available methods

The current GUI provides:

| Method | Typical use |
|---|---|
| `kNN` | Local similarity-based imputation; current default |
| `RF` | Random-forest based imputation |
| `Mean` | Column/feature mean strategy, useful mainly as a simple baseline |
| `Median` | Robust central-value strategy |
| `Zero` | Explicit zero filling; use only when zero has a valid interpretation |
| `Minimum` | Low-value replacement strategy |

Method choice should be justified by the expected missingness mechanism and downstream analysis.

## GUI workflow

1. Click **Load data**.
2. Click **Visualize missing values** before changing the matrix.
3. Inspect the original table and missingness visualization.
4. Select an imputation **Method**.
5. Click **Run imputation**.
6. Compare original and imputed distributions.
7. Download the diagnostic plots if they are part of the analysis record.

::: {.callout-important}
## Default does not mean universally correct
`kNN` is the interface default, but no imputation method is optimal for every proteomics design. Report the selected method in the Methods section of a manuscript and preserve the pre-imputation data for auditability.
:::

## Output

The imputed state is stored in the active project object and in:

```text
Step5_data_imputation.rda
```

Continue with [Data normalization](data_normalization.qmd).
